full_judgment: 14. Regarding the dakhilas the Court of appeal below held that by dakhilas Exhibits A (9)-A(17) the defendants are found to have paid rents in the names of Saku Sarder and Hossain Sarder. That means the names of Saku Sarder and Hossain Sarder stand recorded in the dakhilas as tenants. The Court of appeal further held that most of these dakhilas are of the years 1341 BS and the dakhila Exhibit A(9) is of the year 1352 BS and had Tayebuddin's name been mutated in the landlord's sherista immediately after execution of alleged document, Exhibit F as claimed by defendants, they would not have paid rents in the names of Saku Sarder and Hossain Sarder by these dakhilas Exhibits A(9)-A(17). The appellate Court further held that the SA khatians Exhibits D(2) and D(3) show that names of defendant No.1 and Gafuran Nessa were recorded in the Khatian but the dakhilas Exhibits A(35)-A(39)are in the name of Tayebuddin. When Tayebuddin was not recorded tenant in the SA khatian how the rent can be put in his name instead of the recorded tenant. For all these reasons, the Court of appeal came to the conclusion that all these dakhilas were managed by defendant No.1 who was a Government Kanongo.
